issues.detail: The Greek 'εβασιλευσεν' is a perfect tense verb (has reigned/reigned), but the Vietnamese translation 'đã trị vì' is placed at the end of the sentence as a subordinate clause following 'Vì' (Because). In the Greek, 'οτι εβασιλευσεν' means 'that [He] has reigned,' which is the content of what is being shouted/said. The Vietnamese structure makes it sound like a reason for saying Hallelujah ('Hallelujah because God... reigned') rather than the content of the shout itself.
